text.title: Competitor Analysis Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the question is a point-in-time baseline or a change-over-time reading, whether a substitution-based competitor set of at least three is nameable, and whether pricing is observable — to a full matrix-and-positioning run, a run with `unknown` price cells, or a skip into competitive-intelligence or market-analysis.

decision-tree.root-question: Is the question what the competitive field looks like right now, or how it has moved since a previous reading?

branch.when: the ask is period-over-period movement — price changes, new entrants, feature launches since last quarter — against an existing baseline

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to competitive-intelligence — this methodology produces a dated snapshot, not a delta series over one

branch.when: no current baseline exists and the ask is a point-in-time picture of who the buyer evaluates
branch.question: Can at least 3 products the buyer would weigh in the same purchase decision be named today, plus at least one non-software substitute (spreadsheet, agency, manual process, doing nothing)?

branch.when: fewer than 3 direct competitors are identifiable, or the substitute side is blank

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to market-analysis or customer discovery to establish what the buyer actually uses instead before building a matrix

branch.when: 3 or more direct competitors are nameable and at least one non-software substitute is known
branch.question: Is pricing published for most of the set, or is it quote-only / "contact sales"?

branch.when: pricing is quote-only or gated for most of the set and no sourced quote is in hand

conclusion.verdict: proceed, but every unpriced cell reads the literal `unknown` — never infer a figure from the vendor's other plans or from segment norms

branch.when: list prices with plan names are published or obtainable and can be dated

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; normalise every price to one unit against a stated reference workload, source and date each cell, then build the positioning map on two uncorrelated buyer criteria
